name: Iron Mountain
key_signal: IRM trades just below its 52-week high with a golden cross and 37% six-month momentum, but has stalled over the last month (-3.4%) while trading at a nosebleed 134x trailing P/E and burning free cash flow (-$499M).
thesis: Iron Mountain's data-center and digital transformation pivot has driven a powerful 6-month rally (+37%), with the stock holding above both its 50- and 200-day moving averages and a golden cross intact—technical hallmarks of a durable uptrend. Revenue growth of 21.6% and operating margins near 21% show the business is scaling, and consensus among the 11 covering analysts is 'buy,' suggesting sell-side confidence hasn't wavered even as the stock approaches its 52-week high of $134.68. The 2.79% dividend yield still offers income support while the growth narrative plays out.
bear_case: The valuation is genuinely difficult to justify on fundamentals alone: a 134x trailing P/E, 46x forward P/E, and a deeply negative price-to-book (-30x, implying negative shareholder equity) leave essentially no margin of safety if sentiment shifts. More concerning, free cash flow is negative (-$499M) despite $7.2B in revenue, meaning the dividend and growth capex are being funded by debt or equity issuance—a fragile setup for a REIT if rates back up or capital markets tighten. The 1-month momentum has already turned negative (-3.4%) and price sits below its 50-day SMA (125.30 vs. spot of 123.82), a possible early warning that the golden-cross uptrend is losing steam right as the stock sits near all-time highs with no valuation cushion.
